intro: Every plant in the botanic garden's glasshouse bloomed on the same night, and the labels in the pots had all been rewritten, though the gardeners say they saw no one enter after closing. The glasshouse at midnight is a cathedral of steam and green noise, root systems knitting in the dark, and the people who tend it know better than to be startled by a change they cannot explain; that is the first lesson of the trade. Each morning the head gardener walks the central aisle with a basket, and at the bottom of it, beneath the fallen petals and the stray snail, lies a folded page torn from yesterday's ledger, one line scored through and written again above it in a hand that is almost, but not quite, her own. She has kept every one of these pages in a wooden box under the bench, and last week, when the new apprentice asked what they were, she only said that plants forgive a great deal, but a record has to be honest.
echo: In Kyoto they hold parties just to watch the trees flower.
